answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism combines recurring proof-of-work with reputation decay. Each identity must pay computation and pass an original peer review every epoch; its prior record is an anchor for weight, not a permanent pass. A lotus-like identity that stops working quickly loses standing, while a fable or copied answer earns no attestations. Because every fake head must repeatedly fund and perform verifiable work, creating thousands of sybils costs more than the rewards they can obtain.
